questionText:
Consider the following matrix:

$$R = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 4 & 8 \\ 1 & 3 & 9 & 27 \\ 1 & 4 & 16 & 64 \\ 1 & 5 & 25 & 125 \end{bmatrix}$$

The absolute value of the product of Eigen values of $R$ is __________.
explanation:
1. Product of Eigenvalues and Determinant:
The product of the eigenvalues of a matrix $R$ is equal to its determinant, i.e., $\prod \lambda_i = \det(R)$.

2. Vandermonde Matrix Structure:
The given matrix $R$ is a $4 \times 4$ Vandermonde matrix of the form:
$R = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & x_1 & x_1^2 & x_1^3 \\ 1 & x_2 & x_2^2 & x_2^3 \\ 1 & x_3 & x_3^2 & x_3^3 \\ 1 & x_4 & x_4^2 & x_4^3 \end{bmatrix}$
where $x_1 = 2, x_2 = 3, x_3 = 4, x_4 = 5$.

3. Determinant Calculation:
The determinant of a Vandermonde matrix is given by the formula:
$\det(R) = \prod_{1 \le i < j \le 4} (x_j - x_i)$

Calculating all pairwise differences $(x_j - x_i)$ for $j > i$:
- $(x_2 - x_1) = 3 - 2 = 1$
- $(x_3 - x_1) = 4 - 2 = 2$
- $(x_4 - x_1) = 5 - 2 = 3$
- $(x_3 - x_2) = 4 - 3 = 1$
- $(x_4 - x_2) = 5 - 3 = 2$
- $(x_4 - x_3) = 5 - 4 = 1$

Multiplying these differences together:
$\det(R) = 1 \times 2 \times 3 \times 1 \times 2 \times 1 = 12$

4. Absolute Value:
The absolute value of the product of eigenvalues is $|\det(R)| = |12| = 12$.
